concept.name: Vector Databases, HNSW Indexing & RAG Pipelines
concept.tagline: Perform high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) similarity search for AI LLM context retrieval.

spark.summary: Vector databases index high-dimensional vector embeddings (e.g. 1536-dim vectors) produced by AI models, enabling sub-millisecond semantic search via Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graph indexing.
spark.keyTakeaway: Use HNSW graph indexing with Cosine Similarity or Dot Product metrics for fast RAG knowledge retrieval.

concept.whyItMatters: Traditional B-Trees and relational indexes cannot search unstructured high-dimensional embeddings. Vector databases bridge LLM context windows with enterprise data.
whenNotToUse: Exact string lookups or traditional SQL primary key relational queries.
keyPoints: Embeddings map text or media into dense numerical vectors in high-dimensional vector space.
HNSW constructs multi-layer navigable small world graphs to achieve logarithmic O(log N) search latency.
RAG combines vector similarity retrieval with generative LLM prompt context.

examples.title: Notion AI Q&A Search
examples.scenario: Searching 50M workspace documents for semantic matches.
examples.outcome: Pinecone/Qdrant retrieves top-5 vector chunks in 12ms.

tradeOffs.pro: Sub-20ms search across billions of vectors.
tradeOffs.con: Approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) trade-off means recall is ~95-99% rather than exact 100%.

failureModes.name: Out-of-Memory Graph Exhaustion
failureModes.description: HNSW graphs require holding node vector indexes in RAM, leading to memory spikes under large datasets.
failureModes.mitigation: Use scalar quantization (SQ8) or product quantization (PQ) memory compression.

commonMistakes: Filtering metadata post-search instead of pre-filtering vector queries.

caseStudy.problem: Retrieving contextually relevant documentation for GPT enterprise models.
caseStudy.solution: Vector embeddings indexed in HNSW vector databases.
caseStudy.impact: Sub-15ms semantic context retrieval across petabyte knowledge bases.

relationships.description: Vector indexing extends classical tree indexing to multi-dimensional vector spaces.

questions.title: HNSW Vector Indexing Mechanics
questions.prompt: Why is HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) preferred over brute-force k-NN (k-Nearest Neighbors) in production RAG systems?

options.text: HNSW converts numerical vectors into plaintext strings.
options.explanation: HNSW builds graph structures over vector embeddings, not plaintext conversion.

options.text: Brute-force k-NN scales linearly O(N), whereas HNSW builds a multi-layer graph that navigates to nearest neighbors in logarithmic O(log N) time.
options.explanation: Correct! HNSW transforms expensive linear scans into sub-millisecond graph traversals.

rubric.excellent: Explains logarithmic graph traversal in HNSW versus linear scan overhead in brute-force k-NN.
rubric.gap: Confuses vector indexing with full-text keyword search.

questions.sampleSolution: HNSW builds multi-layer graph skips to achieve logarithmic O(log N) vector similarity search.
questions.explanation: Brute-force vector distance calculation across millions of vectors stalls CPU execution.

interviewProblems.title: Enterprise RAG Knowledge Assistant Architecture
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: You are building an AI assistant querying 10,000,000 corporate documents with strict per-tenant data isolation. How do you design the vector ingestion, indexing, and RAG retrieval pipeline?

dimensions.name: Metadata Pre-Filtering & Tenant Isolation
dimensions.description: Pre-filtering HNSW vector searches by tenant_id payload.

dimensions.name: Chunking & Quantization
dimensions.description: Using 512-token semantic chunking with scalar quantization.

interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Chunk documents into 512-token segments and generate 1536-dim OpenAI embeddings. Store in a Qdrant/Pinecone cluster with pre-filtered HNSW metadata namespace per tenant. Cache frequent prompt context in Redis.
commonPitfalls: Post-filtering tenant boundaries after ANN graph traversal, risking cross-tenant data leakage.
